Te Kāhui Kaumātua

"We are watchers. We are each other's guardians.
We are attuned to our bodies and environments.
We shift with the mauri."
Why We Do This

I saw the pattern. Nanny and Papa. Uncle Steve. Uncle Harry. Strong people, strong whakapapa — but over time, strength faded, mobility was lost, life was limited.

Our tūpuna were navigators. They watched the signs and adjusted their course. When I saw the same signs appearing in Mum, Dad and Uncle James, I changed ours. Not on my watch.

My Philosophy

Strength is resilience — commanding oneself to complete a task, physically or mentally. Barriers and obstacles are expected in life. If life's barriers are only weights to be lifted, we can progress our way there, one lift at a time.

Quick Start

Your Progress

Text Size

Preparation

We have the plan, now prepare. Focus the mind, visualise the movements. Feel the spirit rise, blood flowing, joints and muscles surging.

Warm-Up — 5 mins

Low resistance. Conversational pace (you can talk easily). Treadmill (walk/jog), bike, or elliptical.

Dynamic Stretches / Mobility — 10 mins

Calf Pumps
  • On the ground or against a wall
  • Alternating legs, pumping
  • Gently push heel to floor
Leg Swings (alternate legs)
  • Stabilise against an object
  • Swing leg forward then backward
  • On backward, try to bring heel to bum
  • Forward = hamstrings, back = quads
  • Start low, go higher each swing
Side Swings (alternate legs)
  • Stabilise against an object
  • Swing leg sideways across body
  • Start low, go higher each swing
Opening / Closing the Gates
  • Stabilise against an object
  • Lift knee out to side
  • Bring knee across then lower to ground
  • Feel the hip socket open, change sides
  • Do movement in reverse (open gate)
Closing the Gate
  • Same stance, reverse the movement
  • Sweep knee back through and across
  • Change sides after a few reps
Trunk Twists (side to side)
  • Facing forward, feet parallel with shoulders
  • Twist to face the rear, then other side
  • Keep feet planted (no pivot) for a few reps, then pivot and twist further
Chest Pumps
  • Start palms down in front, swing out elbows bent x2
  • Arms front palms up, swing out arms straight
Shoulder Swings
  • Starting small, swing arms forward in circles
  • Bigger circles as the shoulders warm up
  • Swing backwards
  • Turn head first, body will follow (prevents dizziness)
Sign

Stiff hips, knees, shoulders or ankles.

Realign

Focus on that area. Start gentle. Move often. Over time it will strengthen and move more freely.

Campfire Kōrero

How do you prepare for a challenge?

Day One: Push

Chest, shoulders & triceps

Dumbbell Incline Bench Press
3 x Sets · 8 x Reps
Note: Keep elbows tucked
Dumbbell Shoulder Press
3 x Sets · 8 x Reps
Note: Keep elbows tucked
Dumbbell Lateral Raises
3 x Sets · 8 x Reps
Note: Keep elbows above hands
Triceps Skull-Crushers
3 x Sets · 8 x Reps
Note: Keep elbows at 90 degrees

Progression / Regression options for any move: +/- reps, +/- sets, slow-count eccentrics, pause-reps, +/- weight.

Sign

Shoulder discomfort or instability.

Realign

Focus on technique. Reduce the weight. Build confidence first.

Campfire Kōrero

What do you do when you're outside your comfort zone?

Day Two: Pull

Back & biceps

Cable Lateral Pull Down
3 x Sets · 8 x Reps
Note: Pull to chest
Single-Arm Rows
3 x Sets · 8 x Reps
Note: Pull to belly-button
Dumbbell Biceps Curls
3 x Sets · 8 x Reps
Note: Alternate arms. Start neutral to supinated grip. Little finger up. Do not move the elbows.

Progression / Regression options for any move: +/- reps, +/- sets, slow-count eccentrics, pause-reps, +/- weight.

Sign

Neck, shoulder or upper-back tension.

Realign

Relax the shoulders. Pull through the back muscles. Reduce weight if needed.

Campfire Kōrero

How did our tūpuna respond to a challenge?

Day Three: Legs

Glutes, quads & hamstrings

Squat
3 x Sets · 8 x Reps
Note: Back straight, hold breath and engage core
Walking Lunges
3 x Sets · 8 x Reps
Note: Keep wide stance. Add rākau if unstable
Romanian Dead-Lifts
3 x Sets · 8 x Reps
Note: Hinge at hip. Keep back straight

Progression / Regression options for any move: +/- reps, +/- sets, slow-count eccentrics, pause-reps, +/- weight.

Sign

Balance feels off or movement feels unstable.

Realign

Slow down. Widen your stance. Use support if needed. Build confidence first.

Campfire Kōrero

What is an adventure to you?

Recovery

Strength is built between sessions. Recovery matters. Sleep matters. Kai matters. Consistency matters.

Kai

Our DNA was shaped by generations of Pasifika explorers eating natural foods of the islands and ocean. Our bodies are high-performance machines, attuned to long voyages on minimal diets. We absorb nutrients fast and hold minerals longer.

Many modern foods are highly processed, energy dense and inflammatory. We are less active than our ancestors and have regular, quick access to food.

Two Questions When Selecting Kai

  • Is it natural to my DNA? This is quality.
  • Is it aligned to my output? This is quantity (caloric & energy density).
Sign

Low energy, poor recovery, inflammation, sore joints or digestive issues.

Realign

Look at what you're eating. Increase water, vegetables, fruit and protein. Reduce highly processed foods. Then listen for new signs — good or bad.

Karakia

E te Atua,
Whakapakari i ō mātou tinana, ō mātou hinengaro, ō mātou wairua.
Kia ārahina mātou e ō mātou tūpuna mō ngā whakatipuranga e haere ake nei.
Haumi e, Hui e, Tāiki e.
Opening karakia — strengthen our bodies, minds and spirits; guide us for generations to come.
E te Atua,
I a mātou e wehe atu ana i tēnei ahi kā, waerea ō mātou tinana, ō mātou hinengaro, ō mātou wairua.
Kia hono tonu mātou i roto i te mauri o tō mātou whakapapa.
Haumi e, Hui e, Tāiki e.
Closing karakia — as we leave this fire, cleanse our bodies, minds and spirits; keep us connected to the mauri of our whakapapa.

Kaitiakitanga

We are each other's kaitiaki. We watch for the signs. We encourage one another. We help adjust course when needed. We draw strength from our tūpuna and help light the path for the generations to come.
